arch_ref_postDisasterDef: RULE: Division A 1.4.1.2 definition 'Post-disaster building', NBC 2020 / BCBC 2024 / VBBL 2025 / NBC(AE) 2023 (local texts data/raw/codes): list 'hospitals, emergency treatment facilities and blood banks, telephone exchanges, power generating stations and electrical substations, control centres for natural gas distribution, control centres for air, land and marine transportation, water treatment facilities, water storage facilities, water and sewage pumping stations, sewage treatment facilities, buildings having critical national defence functions, and buildings of the following types, unless exempted ... : emergency response facilities, fire, rescue and police stations ..., and communications facilities, including radio and television stations'. BCBC: 'a building that the authority having jurisdiction has determined is necessary for the provision of essential services to the general public in the event of a disaster and includes buildings meeting these criteria but not limited to'; VBBL: 'the Chief Building Official has determined'; NBC and NBC(AE): no 'determined' wording. No shelter, reception centre or data centre named. BCBC Note A-1.4.1.2.(1): 'Some municipalities have emergency management plans that specify which buildings are to be used for the provision of essential services after a disaster ... If in doubt ... designers should consult with the authority having jurisdiction.' — bcbc2024.txt lines 2232-2251, 2963-2979; vbbl2025_v1.txt 1769; nbc.txt 1858; nbc_ab2023.txt 2121
arch_ref_nbcT4121: RULE: Table 4.1.2.1 Importance Categories for Buildings, and Notes A-4.1.2.1.(3) and A-Table 4.1.2.1, Division B, NBC 2020 / BCBC 2024 / VBBL 2025 / NBC(AE) 2023 (identical wording): High = 'Community centres and elementary, middle and secondary schools are High Importance Category buildings.'; Post-disaster = 'A post-disaster building.' A-4.1.2.1.(3): 'In a building containing more than one major occupancy and classified in more than one Importance Category, the classification of each independent structural system shall be the same as for any part of the building that is dependent on that structural system and for the highest usage group'. A-Table 4.1.2.1: community centres explained in the NRC Structural Commentaries (not read). Phrase 'emergency shelter' absent from all four texts. — bcbc2024.txt 28442-28472, 35008-35050; nbc.txt 27158, 34061; nbc_ab2023.txt 32856; vbbl2025_v1.txt 21016-21037, 25774

arch_ref_emergPower: RULE: Subsection 3.2.7, Division B, NBC 2020 / BCBC 2024 / VBBL 2025 / NBC(AE) 2023 (same wording): 3.2.7.4.(1)(b) emergency lighting power 'i) 2 h for a building within the scope of Subsection 3.2.6., ii) 1 h for a building of Group B ..., iii) 1 h for a building constructed in accordance with Article 3.2.2.51. or 3.2.2.60., and iv) 30 min for a building of any other occupancy'; 3.2.7.3.(1)(i) emergency lighting in A-2 floor areas with occupant load 60 or more; 3.2.7.5.(1) emergency supply installed to CSA C282; 3.2.7.8.(3) fire alarm 24 h supervisory then 30 min (5 min without annunciator); 3.2.7.9.(1) 2 h generator only for elevators in buildings over 36 m, fire-suppression water supply, 3.2.6 air-quality and venting fans. No clause requires heating, cooling or filtration on emergency power. — bcbc2024.txt 15358-15500; nbc.txt 15108-15182; nbc_ab2023.txt 13816-13886; vbbl2025_v1.txt 10656-10705

arch_ref_vbblPart13: RULE: Vancouver Building By-law 2025, Book I, Part 13 Temporary Buildings and Temporary Uses (consolidated 5 May 2026): 13.1.1.2.(1) applies to '(a) temporary buildings, including ... emergency shelters in temporary buildings ... (c) temporary uses in existing buildings designed to support a different major occupancy, including ... emergency shelters'; 13.1.1.3.(1) measures 'do not apply to new work, which must conform to the requirements for new construction'; 13.1.1.5.(1) temporary = not more than 12 consecutive months or a fixed term no longer than 3 years acceptable to the CBO; 13.4.4.1.(1) 'Notwithstanding the provisions of this By-law, a temporary emergency shelter is permitted in an existing building' with no cooking except microwave reheating, 1 staff per 20 shelter spaces, 1 bed per 3.7 m2 (2 if bunks), 900 mm aisles both sides, at least 2 means of egress, exit signs, smoke alarms throughout, 1 WC per 20 spaces, 1 lavatory per 5 WC, staff first-aid training; 13.4.4.1.(2) fixed-term shelter up to 3 years if sprinklered (quick response or residential), single-stage fire alarm, operating agreement acceptable to the CBO — vbbl2025_v1.txt 36565-36615, 36794-36822
